assessments.reasoning: The GitHub Git object API for spdx/license-list-data identifies annotated object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b as v3.29.0. Its object.type is commit and object.sha is 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, the revision used by the 1.0 detail. Verification reports unsigned.

At that commit, json/details/NLOD-1.0.json has licenseId NLOD-1.0, name “Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD) 1.0” and isDeprecatedLicenseId false. Both crossRef[0].url and seeAlso[0] contain http://data.norge.no/nlod/en/1.0. The separate comment labels /nlod/no/1.0 as a translation.

The Agency's HTTPS English page at the referenced host and path names NLOD 1.0, and §10 expressly permits a reservation to version 1.0. The captured digest matches the 1.0 publisher revision. This supports the identity of the destination in its assigned context role. SPDX controls the identifier assignment.

challenge.method: Compared the annotated object's target with the detail URL commit, then checked the JSON fields and compared both English reference fields with both publisher editions. Tested a substituted 2.0 path, a different publisher, the Norwegian comment link and an inference of text equality.
challenge.results: Both English references specify data.norge.no/nlod/en/1.0. Only the scheme differs from the inspected HTTPS locator. The 2.0 substitution fails the path, title and §10 checks. The Agency metadata establishes the publisher at the matching destination. The crossRef field records match as the string “false”, so it supplies no positive text-match result. These facts support the documentary link.

limitations: The tag is unsigned. Repository provenance supports the object-to-commit reading. Signer authentication and the present value of a mutable tag ref were not established.
The HTTP reference was compared with the HTTPS original by host and path. Redirect behavior, historical HTTP response bytes, text equivalence and XML build lineage were not verified.
The Norwegian translation link does not resolve the reported versioning discrepancy. Compatibility, approvals and grants for particular works fall outside the correspondence.
reasoning: SPDX Data v3.29.0 points to the commit containing the NLOD-1.0 detail. Its identifier, name and English publisher reference agree with the Agency's 1.0 edition. SCES §7 requires an external assertion to be attributed to its owning index and pinned to an exact release or record. Protocol stage 7 requires reopening the sources and challenging scope and counterexamples. The tag establishes the release revision, the detail establishes SPDX's assertion, and the Agency document independently identifies the referenced edition.
